name: reviewbench-seed-v1
description: A hand-audited seed corpus that separates parser-model evidence from reviewer priority, including source-observable trivia changes that a CST-only policy must not deprioritize.

label_policy.syntax_preserved: The current parser/model sees the same non-trivia syntax. This is a factual evidence label, not a claim of unchanged behavior or lower priority.
label_policy.behavior_sensitive: The mutation can change observable behavior, so its attention priority must remain review_first even when its evidence class is syntax_preserved.

known_limitations: Seed-sized and hand-authored; it is not statistically representative of GitHub pull requests.
Labels are based on language semantics and manual inspection, not execution against project test suites.

Cases are isolated single-file snippets and do not cover cross-file effects, generated code, dependencies, or build configuration; one C stringification case is only an adversarial sentinel, not broad preprocessor coverage.
The corpus checks evidence classification and conservative attention priority only; it does not measure reviewer time saved or defect-detection recall.

cases.after:
def total(left, right):
    return left + right
cases.rationale: Spaces around the binary operator are Python trivia and do not alter the parsed program.

cases.before:
def within_quota(used, limit):
    return used <= limit
cases.after:
def within_quota(used, limit):
    return used < limit
cases.rationale: Changing <= to < rejects the boundary value where used equals limit.
Python debug f-strings preserve expression-source whitespace, changing output from 'x=1' to 'x =1' while the current CST predicate still matches.
Spacing changes between the same JavaScript tokens do not alter the parsed program.
Changing conjunction to disjunction broadens access to callers satisfying only one condition.

cases.after: export function discount(price: number, rate: number): number { return price * rate; }
cases.rationale: Spacing changes around type annotations and operators leave TypeScript syntax unchanged.
Replacing the fallback literal disables retries when no value is configured.

cases.after: pub fn total(left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 { left + right }
cases.rationale: Rust ignores the changed spacing between the same tokens.
Replacing subtraction with addition reverses how the fee affects the returned amount.
Rust stringify! preserves this token spacing in its result, so the constant changes from 'a+b' to 'a + b' while the current CST predicate still matches.

cases.before: final class Limit{static int clamp(int value){return value;}}
cases.after: final class Limit { static int clamp(int value) { return value; } }
cases.rationale: Whitespace is added between the same Java tokens without changing the parse tree.
Removing logical negation inverts the authorization decision.
Spacing and indentation change while all Go syntax tokens stay fixed.
Changing < to <= performs one additional retry at the configured boundary.
JSON ignores whitespace outside string values, and the parsed value tokens stay fixed.
Replacing the boolean value changes the configuration represented by the document.
The C preprocessor stringification operator observes token spacing even when the Tree-sitter CST is unchanged.
Whitespace between inline elements changes rendered text from 'ab' to 'a b' even though the current Tree-sitter representation is unchanged.
